claims.text: Post-synthesis controlled annealing can tune the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Post-synthesis controlled annealing can tune the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Controlled annealing promotes short-range atomic ordering in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Short-range atomic ordering modulates magnetic exchange interactions.
The as-cast non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy has a largely random atomic distribution.
Selected annealing temperatures and durations can induce measurable short-range order without causing phase separation.
Annealing changes the local atomic environment through the development of short-range order.
Annealing facilitates atomic rearrangements that alter interatomic distances and local bonding.
Changes in interatomic distances and local bonding alter magnetic exchange pathways.
Altered magnetic exchange pathways shift the magnetic transition temperature.
Altered magnetic exchange pathways change the magnetocaloric response.
Controlled annealing will systematically shift magnetic transition temperatures relative to the as-cast condition.
Controlled annealing will enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to the as-cast condition.
Excessive annealing can cause phase segregation or grain coarsening.
Annealing-induced phase segregation or grain coarsening can deteriorate the targeted magnetocaloric properties.
